title: Nalyvaiko Uprising
capsule: The Nalyvaiko Uprising (1594–1596) was a Zaporozhian Cossack rebellion in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth led by Severyn Nalyvaiko, a registered Cossack who turned against the Commonwealth after campaigns in Moldavia. Operating alongside Hryhoriy Loboda and Matviy Shaula, Nalyvaiko's forces swept across right-bank Ukraine and Belarus, sacking Lutsk, Mogilev, and Slutsk before Polish hetman Stanisław Żółkiewski cornered them near Lubny in spring 1596. After a two-week siege, the Cossacks surrendered Nalyvaiko; he was taken to Warsaw and executed—drawn and quartered—in 1597, while the Sejm annulled the registered Cossack register and magnates redistributed confiscated Cossack lands.

The uprising is attested in Polish chronicles and Cossack registers, but the geographic control exercised by the rebels at any given moment is approximate and based on narrative sources rather than administrative maps.
